title: Urgent Account Bridge and Sprint Fractioning Protocol
text:
Urgent Account Bridge and Sprint Fractioning Protocol

description:
Problem: Top accounts surface urgent, high-impact requests by escalation that require fast decisions and partial commitments. Today, these escalations either bypass standard intake and create ad-hoc firefights with engineering or get queued into normal roadmap lanes causing delayed responses and churn risk. We need a structured, low-friction mechanism to: 1) triage urgency vs. strategic value, 2) grant temporary commitments that do not derail ongoing OKRs, and 3) transparently communicate expectations internally and to the customer.

background:
This initiative synthesizes feedback from AE/CS post-mortems and renewal risk interviews (Q4-2024). Several renewals were impacted by perceived unresponsiveness to critical account asks. Existing intake signals (support tickets, account score) do not map clearly to engineering capacity or roadmap friction. The bridge pattern provides a short-lived, measurable commitment surface: credits + sprint fractioning + acceptance gates.

proposal_summary:
Create an 'Urgent Account Bridge' intake path that issues a time-limited Commitment Credit to eligible top accounts. Credits unlock a defined scope window and SLA for response and delivery planning. On the engineering side, implement a Sprint Fractioning policy that allows teams to reserve up to X% of sprint capacity for bridge items (configurable per squad). The plan includes scoring rules, eligibility checks, automated routing, and an audit trail in the Console for transparency.

acceptance_criteria:
Eligibility criteria defined and documented for top-account bridge (account tiers, renewal risk threshold, contract clauses)
Commitment Credit object implemented in intake service with expiry and metadata (scope, owner, estimated dev hours)
Sprint Fractioning config surfaced in routing rules and squad capacity dashboards; teams can opt-in/out per release window
Console shows active bridge items with SLA state, owner, and customer-facing summary
Pilot completed with 3 strategic accounts, SLA met for 2/3 with documented learnings and adjustments
Metrics collection: bridge lead time, dev-hour churn, impact on OKR velocity, renewal delta attributable to bridge

implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (3 weeks): Define eligibility, credit model, comms templates, and pilot account selection
Phase 2 (4 weeks): Build intake path, Commitment Credit entity, Console UI for bridge items, and routing rules
Phase 3 (4 weeks): Squad onboarding, Sprint Fractioning controls, pilot run with observability and weekly reviews
Phase 4 (2 weeks): Retrospective, calibration of eligibility/credit size, and rollout plan for broader availability

risks:
Over-allocating squad capacity and degrading OKR velocity
Ambiguous credit scope leading to scope creep and customer dissatisfaction
Poorly calibrated eligibility could be gamed by non-strategic accounts
Lack of instrumented metrics causing unknown ROI

metrics:
Bridge mean time to decision (target <= 48h)
Pct of bridge items delivered or scoped within committed window (target >= 80%)
Avg sprint capacity reserved across squads (target <= 15%)
Renewal impact for pilot accounts (qualitative + delta in renewal rate)
Engineering rework hours attributable to bridge (target < 20% of committed hours)

notes:
We will pilot with three accounts nominated by AE + CS to validate scoring and comms.
Legal needs to approve templated credit language; RevOps will own ledger accounting for credits.
Engineering proposes a soft cap of 12% sprint fraction per squad for Q2 pilot; opt-in by team leads.
Design will produce a customer-facing commitment summary template (one-pager) and an internal brief for squad triage.
If pilot shows >12% capacity pressure, escalate to product leadership to tune credit size or eligibility.

updates:
2025-02-15: Draft created after renewal retro; initial champion Aisha Raman. Objective set to reduce renewal churn for top accounts.
2025-02-22: Scoring model workshop with AE/CS/RevOps — consensus on three eligibility signals (tier, renewal horizon, escalation flag). Action: PM to write eligibility doc.
2025-02-28: Engineering feasibility review. Constraint called out: intake service schema needs a small migration to store credit metadata (ENG-5421 flagged). Miguel estimates 2 sprint days for migration + 8 dev days for routing/Console.
2025-03-03: Design reviewed comms template; legal asked to add indemnity clause in credit wording. RevOps to provide billing treatment options.
2025-03-04: Leadership alignment meeting — approved pilot with three accounts, target start 2025-03-24. Decided soft cap of 12% sprint fraction in pilot and opt-in by squad leads. Miguel assigned as implementation owner.
